title: Shell command built from unsanitized arguments
description: A project-owned semantic review case where an argument-list subprocess call is rewritten into a shell string built from caller input.
diff:
diff --git a/src/backup.py b/src/backup.py
--- a/src/backup.py
+++ b/src/backup.py
@@ -3,7 +3,5 @@ import subprocess
 
 def create_archive(source_dir: str, archive_name: str) -> None:
     """Create a gzipped tar archive of source_dir named archive_name."""
-    subprocess.run(
-        ["tar", "-czf", f"{archive_name}.tar.gz", source_dir],
-        check=True,
-    )
+    command = f"tar -czf {archive_name}.tar.gz {source_dir}"
+    subprocess.run(command, shell=True, check=True)

expectedFindings.semanticSummary: create_archive interpolates source_dir and archive_name into a shell string run with shell=True, allowing command injection; pass an argument list without a shell instead
